problem:
The level curves of the function $f(x,y)=xy$ are given by $f(x,y)=c.$ Which of the following statements are true?

- $c=1$ gives a hyperbola
- $c=-1$ gives a parabola
- $c=0$ gives the axes $x=0$ and $y=0$

feedback.problem: Which of the following represents the level curves of $f(x,y)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The level curves for the function $f(x,y)$ are given by the equations 

$$
f(x,y)=c.
$$

Notice that the range of $f(x,y)$ is $[0,\infty ).$ So, we will consider only level curves for $c\ge 0.$

Therefore, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =c \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} & =c \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={c}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
